title: map/filter/reduce in realistic examples
learningObjectives: Explain map/filter/reduce in realistic examples and use JavaScript collections and iteration safely.

understand.concept: map transforms each array item into a corresponding result; filter keeps items that pass a predicate; reduce combines items into one accumulated result. These methods return values and should be used according to the transformation being expressed.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the right method makes data pipelines clearer and reduces manual indexing logic. Keep callbacks focused and avoid using reduce when map or filter communicates intent more clearly.
understand.analogy: map changes each item, filter selects items, and reduce combines many items into one result.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; collection identity, iteration, and binary storage follow JavaScript specification rules.

explain.narrative: filter selects paid orders, reduce totals their amounts, and map formats their totals as labels.

examples.explanation: filter selects paid orders, reduce totals their amounts, and map formats their totals as labels.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the collection, iteration, or copying behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Build a report from an array of course purchases: filter completed items, map titles, and reduce the total price.
practise.independentTask: Choose an appropriate collection or iteration technique for a small data task. Test duplicates, ordering, identity, and copying behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates its receiver.
Remember that object equality is based on identity.
Use typed arrays only when binary data semantics are needed.

questions.prompt: Which method combines an array into a single accumulated result?
questions.explanation: reduce calls a reducer callback to build one accumulated result.
